full_text_zh:
[P1] 反客为主

[P2] 唐朝时，北方将领仆固怀恩反叛了大唐。他在西域四处游说，联络吐蕃、回纥等十几个小国，集合三十多万大军，气势汹汹地向大唐的都城长安攻过来。他们接连胜利，一个月就打到了离长安只有五十里的泾阳。

[P3] 大唐皇帝赶紧把禁军调进皇宫保护自己。他还让人四处抓壮丁，派重兵把守长安城门。
但是，只守不攻，怎么能赶走敌人呢？皇帝紧急召回六十多岁的老将郭子仪，叫他到泾阳去平乱。可是，郭子仪手下没有兵，只得七拼八凑了一万人马，急急忙忙地赶往泾阳城。

[P4] 到了泾阳，郭子仪还没来得及部署兵力，就被西域的联军包围了。他们兵强马壮，在城外围了一层又一层。放眼望去，漫山遍野都是吐蕃、回纥的士兵，他们的旗帜遮住了天空，兵器寒光闪闪。唐军想找个缝儿突围出去？没门儿！难道大唐神将郭子仪，就要在这小小的泾阳城打败仗了吗？

[P5] 正在这危急关头，仆固怀恩生病去世了。西域的联军没有了总指挥，吐蕃跟回纥便争着当统帅。可是，吐蕃和回纥谁也不服谁，一时分不出胜负。两军只好把兵马分开。吐蕃驻扎在泾阳城的东门外，回纥驻扎在泾阳城的西门边。

[P6] 郭子仪安排好泾阳城的四面防守，就带着两百人马前去探察敌情。出了西门，他一会儿观察地形，一会儿点数回纥营帐，估算回纥军的人数，来来回回跑了好几趟。
守营的回纥军士看着这位胡子花白，身体却很强壮的老将军，忍不住好奇地喊话：
"大唐是哪位将军出战？"

[P7] "郭子仪，郭元帅！"唐军士兵大声回答道。
"郭子仪还活着？"回纥军士大吃一惊，忙又追问道，"那大唐的天可汗呢？也还健在吗？"
"嗨，你这回纥人，说的是什么话！我们的皇帝身体好着呢！"唐军士兵齐声喝道。

[P8] "仆固怀恩欺骗了我们！"回纥军士听了唐军的回答，大叫一声，扭头跑去了主将营帐。唐军的士兵也将这件事报告了郭子仪。郭子仪觉得很奇怪，仆固怀恩到底说了什么谎话呢？当天，他便派使者到回纥军营，求见回纥都督药葛罗。

[P9] 使者对药葛罗说："郭元帅让我来问您，您曾跟随他上过战场，并肩作战，为什么现在却来攻打大唐？这对您有什么好处呢？" 药葛罗却疑惑地问道："他真的在泾阳吗，你不是骗我的吧？假如他在这里的话，可以让我见见他吗？"

[P10] 郭子仪听了使者的回报，决定亲自去回纥军营走一趟：见一见药葛罗。众将军惊得叫起来："回纥人如狼似虎，您怎么能自己送上门去呢？只怕是有去无回呀！"郭子仪摆摆手说："回纥军的人数是我们的几十倍，硬碰硬我们不是对手。过去，我跟药葛罗交情深厚，我孤身前去劝说他，才能不战而胜呀！"

[P11] 他推开房门往外走，出门却看到五百骑兵牵着马，紧握战刀，整整齐齐地排列在门外。
见郭子仪出来，五百骑兵齐声高喊："请让我们保护您。"
"不行，带这么多人去，会坏事的！"说完，郭子仪翻身上马，出了西城门，身后只跟着二三十名亲兵。

[P12] 来到回纥军营外，郭子仪手下的士兵们大声喊道："郭元帅来啦！请回纥首领出来相见！"
"真的假的？"药葛罗害怕有诈，让弓箭手拉弓对准了马上的人。
郭子仪翻身下马，"哐啷"一声，将手中的长戟扔在地上，摘下头盔，脱掉铠甲，大声说道："药葛罗，大唐待回纥不薄，你为什么要跟着仆固怀恩一起叛乱呢？"

[P13] 药葛罗目不转睛地盯着来人，
只见此人虎目圆睁，威风凛凛，
便大喊道："啊，真的是您！"
药葛罗急忙上前，下拜行礼，
郭子仪拉住他的胳膊说："我今天前来，就是为了劝你悬崖勒马。你可以杀了我，但大唐的将士绝不会放过你！"

[P14] 药葛罗不好意思地说："您别这样说！我们是上了仆固怀恩的当，以为天可汗和郭元帅您都去世了，中原没有主人，这才跟着他来到了长安。现在知道您还在，我哪会同您打仗呢？"郭子仪趁机说："吐蕃今天能打大唐，明天就能打回纥。不如你跟我联合起来，这样既能抗击吐蕃，又能与大唐交好。如此天赐良机，不能错过呀！"

[P15] 听说大唐与回纥结了盟，
吐蕃大军吓得连夜卷着
帐篷撤走了。郭子仪与
回纥联合追击，直打得
吐蕃大败而逃。

药葛罗马上命人取来酒，郭
子仪和他一人端起一碗，洒
在地上，对天起誓：大唐与
回纥结盟，共抗吐蕃，两国
友谊久天长。

[P16] 郭子仪一到泾阳，就被吐蕃和回纥的联军围住了。这时候，吐蕃和回纥像凶恶的主人，唐军像弱小的客人，只能被动挨打。后来，郭子仪瓦解了吐蕃和回纥的联盟，就像让他们分了家。唐军和回纥结盟，组成了"新家"，从客人变成了主人，这才主动出击，追赶吐蕃军。这样的计策，就叫作"反客为主"。
full_text_en:
[P1] Turn the tables

[P2] During the Tang Dynasty, the northern general Pu Gu Huai'en rebelled against the Tang Empire. He traveled around the Western Regions, persuading and uniting small states such as Tubo and Huige, gathering an army of over 300,000 troops. With overwhelming momentum, they advanced toward Chang'an, the capital of the Tang Dynasty. After a series of victories, they reached Jingyang, just fifty li away from Chang'an, within a month.

[P3] The Tang emperor quickly moved the imperial guards into the palace to protect himself. He also ordered people to be conscripted from all over and sent heavy troops to guard the gates of Chang'an.
But how could they drive away the enemy by only defending? The emperor urgently recalled the elderly general Guo Ziyi, who was over sixty, and ordered him to go to Jingyang to quell the rebellion. However, Guo Ziyi had no troops under his command, so he could only hastily gather one thousand soldiers and rushed to Jingyang City.

[P4] When they reached Jingyang, Guo Ziyi hadn't even had time to deploy his troops when they were surrounded by the allied forces from the Western Regions. Their army was strong and their horses powerful, encircling the city layer upon layer. Looking out, the hills and fields were filled with soldiers from Tubo and Huige; their banners covered the sky, and their weapons gleamed coldly. Could the Tang army find a crack to break out? No way! Could the great Tang general Guo Ziyi really be defeated in this tiny city of Jingyang?

[P5] At this critical moment, Pu Gu Huai'en fell ill and died. Without a commander, the allied forces from the Western Regions began to compete for leadership between the Tubo and the Uyghurs. However, neither the Tubo nor the Uyghurs would yield to the other, and they could not decide a winner. The two armies could only split their troops. The Tubo camped outside the eastern gate of Jingyang City, while the Uyghurs camped outside the western gate.

[P6] Guo Ziyi arranged the defense of the four sides of Jingyang City, then led two hundred men to scout the enemy situation. After leaving the west gate, he sometimes observed the terrain, sometimes counted the Huihe tents, estimating the number of Huihe troops, going back and forth several times.
The Huihe soldiers guarding the camp looked at this old general with white beard but strong body, and couldn't help but curiously shout:
"Which general of the Tang Dynasty is coming out to fight?"

[P7] "Guo Ziyi, General Guo!" the Tang soldiers shouted back.
"Guo Ziyi is still alive?" the Uyghur soldiers were greatly surprised and hurriedly asked, "And what about the Heavenly Khan of the Great Tang? Is he still alive?"
"Hey, you Uyghur, what are you talking about! Our emperor is in good health!" the Tang soldiers shouted in unison.

[P8] "Puguhuain has deceived us!" The Uyghur soldier, upon hearing the Tang army's response, shouted loudly and turned to run to the general's tent. The Tang soldiers reported this incident to Guo Ziyi. Guo Ziyi felt very puzzled: what lies had Puguhuain told? That day, he sent an envoy to the Uyghur camp to request an audience with the Uyghur commander Yaoke Luo.

[P9] The envoy said to Yaoke Luo: "General Guo sent me to ask you: you once fought side by side with him on the battlefield. Why are you now attacking the Tang Dynasty? What benefit is there for you?" Yaoke Luo asked doubtfully: "Is he really in Jingyang? Are you not deceiving me? If he is here, can I meet him?"

[P10] Guo Ziyi, after hearing the messenger's report, decided to go to the Huihe army camp himself: to meet Yaoke Luo. The generals cried out in shock: "The Huihe are as fierce as wolves and tigers. How can you go there alone? It's likely you won't return!" Guo Ziyi waved his hand and said: "The Huihe army's numbers are dozens of times ours. If we fight head-on, we are no match. In the past, I had a deep friendship with Yaoke Luo. If I go alone to persuade him, we can win without fighting!"

[P11] He pushed open the door and stepped out, only to see five hundred cavalrymen leading their horses, gripping their swords tightly, standing in neat rows outside the door.
When Guo Ziyi appeared, the five hundred cavalrymen shouted in unison: "Let us protect you!"
"No, bringing so many people will ruin things!" He said, then mounted his horse, left through the west gate, followed by only two or three dozen soldiers.

[P12] Outside the Huihe army camp, the soldiers under Guo Ziyi shouted loudly: "General Guo is here! Please let the Huihe leader come out to meet us!"
"Is this real or a trick?" Yageluo, fearing a deception, ordered his archers to aim their bows at the man on horseback.
Guo Ziyi dismounted, with a "clang," threw his long halberd to the ground, removed his helmet, took off his armor, and shouted loudly: "Yageluo, the Tang Dynasty has treated the Huihe well. Why are you following Pu Gu Huai'en in rebellion?"

[P13] Yao Geluo stared intently at the newcomer,
seeing this man with fierce eyes and a commanding presence,
he shouted: "Ah, it really is you!"
Yao Geluo hurried forward and bowed respectfully.
Guo Ziyi grabbed his arm and said: "I have come today to urge you to turn back before it's too late. You may kill me, but the soldiers of the Tang Dynasty will never forgive you!"

[P14] Yao Geluo said awkwardly, "Please don't say that! We were deceived by Pu Gu Huaian. We thought the Heavenly Khan and General Guo had both passed away, and with no ruler in the Central Plains, we followed him to Chang'an. Now that we know you are still alive, how could I possibly fight against you?" Guo Ziyi seized the opportunity and said, "If the Tubo can attack the Tang today, they can attack the Huihe tomorrow. Why not join forces with me? This way, we can resist the Tubo together and maintain good relations with the Tang. Such a heavenly opportunity must not be missed!"

[P15] Hearing that the Tang and the Uyghurs had formed an alliance, 
the Tibetan army was so frightened that they hastily packed up 
their tents and retreated. Guo Ziyi and the Uyghurs joined forces 
to pursue them, defeating the Tibetans decisively.

Yao Geluo immediately ordered wine to be brought. 
Guo Ziyi and he each took a bowl, poured it on the ground, 
and swore to heaven: The Tang and the Uyghurs form an alliance 
to resist the Tibetans; the friendship between our two nations 
shall last forever.

[P16] When Guo Ziyi arrived at Jingyang, he was surrounded by the allied forces of Tubo and Huihe. At that time, Tubo and Huihe were like cruel hosts, while the Tang army was like a weak guest, forced to endure attacks passively. Later, Guo Ziyi broke the alliance between Tubo and Huihe, as if making them split up. The Tang army and Huihe formed an alliance, creating a new 'home,' turning from guests into hosts, and then launched an active attack to chase the Tubo army. This strategy is called 'turning the guest into the host.'
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页标题为“反客为主”，配图是一位骑马持矛的古代武将，画面简洁，突出主题。
[P2] 本页讲述了唐朝将领仆固怀恩反叛，联合西域多国，率三十万大军进攻长安，并在一个月内推进至距长安仅五十里的泾阳。
[P3] 本页描述了唐朝皇帝为应对叛军进攻而紧急调兵守城，并召回老将郭子仪率少量兵力前往泾阳平乱的情景。
[P4] 本页描绘了郭子仪率军抵达泾阳后，尚未部署兵力即被西域联军重重包围的危急情景，画面展现城楼守军与城外敌军对峙，文字强调敌军势大、唐军突围无望，引发对郭子仪能否取胜的疑问。
[P5] 本页描述了仆固怀恩病逝后，西域联军因指挥权之争而分裂，吐蕃与回纥各自驻扎在泾阳城东西门外，形成对峙局面。
[P6] 郭子仪率少量兵力抵达泾阳后，亲自侦察敌情，反复观察地形和敌军营帐。回纥士兵见其年迈却健壮，好奇询问其身份，不知其为大唐名将。
[P7] 郭子仪率军抵达泾阳后，被回纥士兵认出，对方惊讶询问其是否还活着以及大唐皇帝的状况，唐军士兵随即回应皇帝安好，场面紧张而充满对峙气氛。
[P8] 回纥军士因得知仆固怀恩欺骗而愤怒，跑回主将营帐；唐军将此事报告郭子仪，郭子仪感到疑惑，并派使者前往回纥军营求见其都督药葛罗。
[P9] 唐军使者向回纥都督药葛罗传达郭子仪的质问，质疑其为何背叛大唐，药葛罗对此表示怀疑，并请求面见郭子仪。
[P10] 郭子仪决定亲自前往回纥军营会见药葛罗，众将因敌军势大而担忧其安危，郭子仪则表示凭借旧日交情可不战而胜。
[P11] 郭子仪准备出城会见回纥都督，五百名骑兵请求随行保护，但他拒绝，仅带二三十名亲兵出城，以示诚意与胆识。
[P12] 郭子仪单骑赴回纥军营，为表诚意，下马脱甲，向回纥首领药葛罗质问其为何背叛大唐，场面紧张对峙。
[P13] 郭子仪单骑赴回纥军营，药葛罗认出他后震惊并下拜，郭子仪拉住其臂，劝其悬崖勒马，并警告若杀他，大唐将士必不会放过药葛罗。
[P14] 药葛罗向郭子仪解释自己受仆固怀恩欺骗，误以为大唐已无主，故率军至长安；郭子仪趁机提出联合对抗吐蕃，以保双方安全。
[P15] 郭子仪与回纥都督药葛罗结盟，共同对抗吐蕃。双方歃血为盟，誓守友好，随后联合追击吐蕃军队，使其大败而逃。
[P16] 本页通过文字和画面总结了郭子仪在泾阳被吐蕃和回纥联军围困后，成功瓦解其联盟、与回纥结盟并反攻吐蕃的经过，并点明此计策为“反客为主”。画面描绘了郭子仪与回纥首领在帐篷内歃血为盟、共饮结盟的场景。
